{"path":"DESIGN-SYSTEM.md","content":"# Design system: Godzilla 1.0.0 Godzilla is the design system for RIFT CMS documentation sites — born from the rift where molten content rises to the surface. Warm volcanic neutrals, magma-orange accents, and a dense, link-heavy, code-heavy layout language built for technical docs (Astro-style hub/detail pages, left navigation, API reference tables, and syntax-styled code blocks). Every page on this site is built from these components and tokens. Use them rather than writing custom markup or styling — hand-rolled equivalents break visual consistency and will not pick up future design-system changes. ## Components ### alert Callout box for notes, warnings, and danger/breaking-change notices inside docs content. | Parameter | Type | Default | Description | |---|---|---|---| | `variant` | string | `info` | One of info, success, warning, danger. | | `title` | string | `Note` | Callout heading. | | `body_html` | html | `This endpoint is deprecated in favor of ` | Callout body content, may include inline links. | **Usage:** variant must match one of the fixed CSS suffixes: info, success, warning, danger. Any other value falls back to the default neutral alert border. ### card Link tile used on hub pages to point at guides, API endpoints, SDKs, or concepts. | Parameter | Type | Default | Description | |---|---|---|---| | `href` | string | `/guides/building-your-first-pipeline` | Destination URL. | | `tag` | string | `Guide` | Short category label shown above the title. | | `title` | string | `Building your first pipeline` | Card title. | | `description` | string | `Learn how to assemble your first data pi` | One or two sentence summary. | **Usage:** Use one card component call per tile on hub/index pages such as Guides hub, API Reference hub, and SDKs hub. ### chip Small inline badge used for version tags and status labels (e.g. v2, Beta, Deprecated). | Parameter | Type | Default | Description | |---|---|---|---| | `label` | string | `v2` | Chip text. | | `variant` | string | `primary` | One of primary, success, warning, danger, info, or omit for neutral. | **Usage:** variant maps directly to a fixed CSS class suffix; unknown values render as the neutral default chip style. ### code-block Syntax-styled code block with filename/language header and copy affordance, used throughout guides and API reference pages. | Parameter | Type | Default | Description | |---|---|---|---| | `filename` | string | `pipeline.config.json` | Optional filename or example label shown in the header. | | `language` | string | `json` | Language label shown top-right. | | `code` | html | `{ "pipeline": "ingest-orders" }` | The pre-formatted code content (already escaped/highlighted markup if needed). | **Usage:** code is inserted verbatim inside a pre/code block; author it as plain text or pre-escaped markup, since there is no runtime syntax highlighter in this template. ### docs-pagination Prev/next page navigation shown at the bottom of docs content. | Parameter | Type | Default | Description | |---|---|---|---| | `prev_href` | string | `/getting-started/installation` | URL of previous page. | | `prev_label` | string | `Installation` | Title of previous page. | | `next_href` | string | `/getting-started/authentication` | URL of next page. | | `next_label` | string | `Authentication` | Title of next page. | **Usage:** Place once at the bottom of any sequential docs page (Getting Started, Guides, API Reference, SDKs). ### docs-toc On-this-page table of contents rendered alongside long docs content. | Parameter | Type | Default | Description | |---|---|---|---| | `items_html` | html | `

Go SDK v2

An idiomatic client for the v2 REST API, for Go 1.20+.

Install

terminal bash 
go get github.com/godzilla/godzilla-go

Create a client

client.go go 
import (
    "os"

    "github.com/godzilla/godzilla-go"
)

client := godzilla.NewClient(os.Getenv("GODZILLA_API_KEY"))

Create a pipeline

Maps directly onto the Pipelines endpoint — see the Building your first pipeline guide for the concepts.

create_pipeline.go go 
pipeline, err := client.Pipelines.Create(ctx, &godzilla.PipelineCreateParams{
    Name:                   "ingest-orders",
    SourceConnectorID:      "conn_pg_orders",
    DestinationConnectorID: "conn_snowflake_dw",
})

Listening for webhooks

The SDK includes a signature-verification helper for webhook payloads:

verify.go go 
isValid := godzilla.VerifyWebhookSignature(payload, signatureHeader, webhookSecret)
Thread safe

The Godzilla client is safe for concurrent use across multiple goroutines and manages its own HTTP transport pool.

🌋 Godzilla Docs
  • Go SDK
  • Node.js SDK
  • Python SDK
  • SDKs

Node.js SDK v2

A thin, typed wrapper around the v2 REST API for Node.js and TypeScript projects.

Install

terminal bash 
npm install @godzilla/sdk

Create a client

client.ts typescript 
import { Godzilla } from "@godzilla/sdk";

const godzilla = new Godzilla({ apiKey: process.env.GODZILLA_API_KEY });

Create a pipeline

Maps directly onto the Pipelines endpoint — see the Building your first pipeline guide for the concepts.

create-pipeline.ts typescript 
const pipeline = await godzilla.pipelines.create({
  name: "ingest-orders",
  sourceConnectorId: "conn_pg_orders",
  destinationConnectorId: "conn_snowflake_dw",
});

Listening for webhooks

The SDK includes a signature-verification helper for webhook payloads:

verify.ts typescript 
import { verifyWebhookSignature } from "@godzilla/sdk";

const isValid = verifyWebhookSignature(rawBody, signatureHeader, webhookSecret);
Retries are built in

The SDK retries idempotent requests (GET, and POST with an Idempotency-Key) automatically on 429 and 5xx responses using the same backoff the API itself uses.

Godzilla Docs © Godzilla Docs. All rights reserved.

client.ts typescript 
import { Godzilla } from "@godzilla/sdk";

const godzilla = new Godzilla({ apiKey: process.env.GODZILLA_API_KEY });

Create a pipeline

Maps directly onto the Pipelines endpoint — see the Building your first pipeline guide for the concepts.

create-pipeline.ts typescript 
const pipeline = await godzilla.pipelines.create({
  name: "ingest-orders",
  sourceConnectorId: "conn_pg_orders",
  destinationConnectorId: "conn_snowflake_dw",
});

Listening for webhooks

The SDK includes a signature-verification helper for webhook payloads:

verify.ts typescript 
import { verifyWebhookSignature } from "@godzilla/sdk";

const isValid = verifyWebhookSignature(rawBody, signatureHeader, webhookSecret);
Retries are built in

The SDK retries idempotent requests (GET, and POST with an Idempotency-Key) automatically on 429 and 5xx responses using the same backoff the API itself uses.

Godzilla has no server to install — it's a hosted platform you reach over the REST API, either directly or through an SDK.

terminal bash 
npm install @godzilla/sdk

  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GODZILLA_API_KEY"

# Godzilla Docs

> Everything you need to build data pipelines on the Godzilla platform.\n
## Pages
- [Authentication](https://localhost:3002/getting-started-authentication): Authenticate API requests with a bearer API key.
- [Changelog](https://localhost:3002/changelog): Recent changes to the Godzilla API and platform.
- [Concepts](https://localhost:3002/concepts): The core building blocks of Godzilla: pipelines, connectors, events, and schemas.
- [Connectors](https://localhost:3002/concepts-connectors): What a connector is in Godzilla: a pre-built integration to a source or destination system, with its own auth and catalog of built-in types.
- [Events](https://localhost:3002/concepts-events): What an event is in Godzilla: the atomic unit of data moving through a pipeline, plus the platform's own lifecycle events.
- [Glossary](https://localhost:3002/glossary): Definitions for Godzilla's core terms, each linking to its full explanation.
- [Godzilla Docs](https://localhost:3002/index): Everything you need to build data pipelines on the Godzilla platform.
- [Installation](https://localhost:3002/getting-started-installation): Install the Godzilla SDK or start calling the REST API directly.
- [Migration guide (v1 → v2)](https://localhost:3002/migration-guide-v1-to-v2): Move an existing v1 integration to the v2 API: cursor pagination, webhooks, and the new error shape.
- [Pipelines](https://localhost:3002/concepts-pipelines): What a pipeline is in Godzilla: a named, versioned workflow that moves data from a source connector through transform steps to a destination.
- [Quickstart](https://localhost:3002/getting-started-quickstart): Go from zero to a running pipeline in five minutes.
- [Release notes archive](https://localhost:3002/release-notes-archive): Older v1-era release notes, superseded by the current changelog.
- [Schemas](https://localhost:3002/concepts-schemas): How event payload shapes are declared, validated, and evolved in Godzilla.
- [Security & compliance overview](https://localhost:3002/security-and-compliance): How Godzilla handles data in transit and at rest, credential storage, and compliance posture.
- [Support / Contact](https://localhost:3002/support): How to reach the Godzilla team for support, sales, or security reports.
- [Troubleshooting / FAQ](https://localhost:3002/troubleshooting): Common problems and fixes across pipelines, connectors, and webhooks.

## apis
- [API Reference](https://localhost:3002/apis/index): The Godzilla v2 REST API: pipelines, connectors, events, webhooks, and rate limits.
- [Connectors endpoint](https://localhost:3002/apis/connectors): Create, list, and rotate credentials for connectors via the v2 REST API.
- [Events endpoint](https://localhost:3002/apis/events): Query and replay events that have flowed through a pipeline via the v2 REST API.
- [Pipelines endpoint](https://localhost:3002/apis/pipelines): Create, list, and manage pipelines via the v2 REST API.
- [Rate limits & errors](https://localhost:3002/apis/rate-limits-errors): Standard-tier rate limits, pagination envelope, and the v2 API's error response shape.
- [Transforms endpoint](https://localhost:3002/apis/transforms): Create and list transform steps within pipelines via the v2 REST API.
- [Webhooks endpoint](https://localhost:3002/apis/webhooks): Subscribe to Godzilla platform lifecycle events over outbound HTTP via the v2 REST API.

## guides
- [Building your first pipeline](https://localhost:3002/guides/building-your-first-pipeline): Create a source connector, a destination connector, and the pipeline that connects them, end to end.
- [Connecting a data source](https://localhost:3002/guides/connecting-a-data-source): Choose the right connector type and authentication method for a new data source.
- [Guides](https://localhost:3002/guides/index): Task-oriented walkthroughs for building, connecting, and operating Godzilla pipelines.
- [Handling errors & retries](https://localhost:3002/guides/handling-errors-and-retries): How Godzilla retries failed events, when they're dead-lettered, and how to replay them.
- [Monitoring & alerts](https://localhost:3002/guides/monitoring-and-alerts): Watch pipeline health and get notified of failures via webhooks before they become incidents.
- [Scheduling & triggers](https://localhost:3002/guides/scheduling-and-triggers): Run a pipeline on a cron schedule or trigger it directly from incoming events.
- [Transforming events in flight](https://localhost:3002/guides/transforming-events-in-flight): Reshape, filter, and enrich events in real time as they move through a pipeline.

## sdks
- [Go SDK](https://localhost:3002/sdks/go): Install and use godzilla-go to manage pipelines and connectors from Go.
- [Node.js SDK](https://localhost:3002/sdks/node-js): Install and use @godzilla/sdk to manage pipelines and connectors from Node.js.
- [Python SDK](https://localhost:3002/sdks/python): Install and use godzilla-sdk to manage pipelines and connectors from Python.
- [SDKs](https://localhost:3002/sdks/index): Official Godzilla client libraries for Go, Node.js, and Python.
